comparison: Both evaluate claims C5, C9-C11, C21 regarding PLD2 catalytic activity and TREK-1 C-terminus requirements for mechanically evoked currents. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C48, C66-C68 (small PLD2-independent current component) in their evaluation and finds it supported, while OpenEval evaluates these claims separately as UNCERTAIN (R10) due to marginal statistical significance.

Both evaluate claims C22-C26 regarding dSTORM imaging showing TREK-1/PLD2 redistribution from GM1 to PIP2 domains after shear. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C2-C3 in this evaluation (general spatial organization claims), while peer review focuses specifically on the post-shear redistribution pattern.

Both evaluate claims C27-C28 regarding PLD2 redistribution and increased activity. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C1, C18-C20 (broader mechanistic context about PLD2 movement between domains), while peer review focuses specifically on the redistribution and activity increase.

Both evaluate claims C29-C32 regarding cholesterol changes and GM1 cluster dynamics. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with quantitative cluster analysis and reversibility data. Peer review finds it UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting verification of the cholesterol assay method either by additional experiments or citations.

Both evaluate claims C33-C35 regarding cholesterol uptake inhibiting TREK-1 activation. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C6 in this evaluation. Both note the consistency between imaging (increased TREK-1/GM1 correlation) and functional (decreased current) data.

Both evaluate claims C7, C36-C37 regarding ex vivo brain slice experiments with SREBP2 knockout mice. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C70-C73 and notes high variability, while peer review accepts the cholesterol depletion approach and dSTORM data without expressing concerns about variability.

Both evaluate claims C38-C39 regarding PLD activity increase with osmotic stretch. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C4, C17, C41-C42 (broader claims about PLD activity and spatial reorganization across multiple mechanical stimuli), while peer review focuses on the osmotic stretch extension of the shear stress findings.

Both evaluate Drosophila behavioral assays (C8, C43-C45). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C89. Both acknowledge that Drosophila lacks TREK-1 homologs, so downstream effectors remain unknown, but accept that the data demonstrate PLD's conserved role in mechanosensitivity.

Both evaluate claims C40-C42 regarding PLD mechanosensitivity in flies. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C74-C75 and emphasizes evolutionary conservation despite absence of TREK-1 homologs. Peer review combines this with behavioral data (C8, C43-C45) in a single evaluation.

Both evaluate claims C51-C52 regarding the shear thinning mechanism for PLD2 release. OpenEval finds it SUPPORTED as a reasonable mechanistic interpretation. Peer review finds it UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly stating the shear thinning claim is confusing and questioning the equivalence to entropy/order and the asymmetric insertion mechanism.

OpenEval R3 evaluates C1, C18-C20, C27-C28 regarding PLD2 redistribution mechanism and finds it SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates C1-C4 as the overall provocative mechanism and finds it SUPPORTED. Both accept the spatial reorganization data, though peer review emphasizes this is one of multiple possible activation pathways.

OpenEval R2 evaluates C2-C3, C22-C26 regarding spatial organization changes and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates C1-C4 as the overall mechanism and finds it SUPPORTED. Both accept the dSTORM evidence, though peer review emphasizes the mechanism modulates rather than exclusively mediates TREK-1 activation.

OpenEval R4 evaluates C4, C17, C38-C39, C41-C42 regarding PLD activity increases and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer R10 evaluates C1-C4 as part of the overall mechanism and finds it SUPPORTED. Both accept the enzymatic activity data and spatial reorganization evidence.

Both evaluate claims C47, C49-C50 regarding direct mechanosensitivity of TREK-1 in reconstituted systems. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C12. Both note these citations provide important context for understanding that PLD2-independent mechanisms exist alongside the PLD2-dependent pathway.

Both evaluate claims C53, C83-C85 regarding rapid activation kinetics. OpenEval finds the evidence UNCERTAIN due to time resolution near instrument limits and lack of precise calibration. Peer review finds it SUPPORTED without raising concerns about temporal resolution or measurement precision.

Both evaluate claims C62, C96-C99 regarding methodological controls for super-resolution imaging artifacts. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Both accept the FRAP validation and consistency between labeling approaches as adequate controls for potential artifacts.

Both evaluate claims C54-C55 regarding basal TREK-1 currents with inactive PLD2. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Both recognize these measurements as important controls demonstrating TREK-1 functionality independent of PLD2-mediated mechanosensitivity.
Both evaluate claims C63-C65 regarding methodological choices (HEK293T cells, overexpression strategy). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Both accept these as standard, well-justified approaches.

Both evaluate claim C87 regarding consistency across cell types. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval also includes C86. Both view the consistency across different cellular systems as strengthening the findings.

Both evaluate background/contextual claims from prior literature (C15-C16, C56-C61, C78). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes additional claims (C57-C59). Both recognize these as established facts providing necessary context rather than novel findings.

OpenEval R10 evaluates C48, C67-C68 regarding small PLD2-independent current component and finds it UNCERTAIN due to marginal statistical significance (p=0.08, p=0.11). Peer R1 includes these same claims in their evaluation of the overall electrophysiology findings and finds them SUPPORTED without expressing concerns about statistical significance.

OpenEval R15 evaluates C14, C66 regarding TREK-1 pressure sensitivity characterization and finds it SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C66 in their broader evaluation of electrophysiology data and finds it SUPPORTED. Both accept these as valid baseline characterizations.

OpenEval R19 evaluates claim C69 (citation to Yuan et al., 2022 regarding spatial separation of lipid domains) and finds it SUPPORTED as providing important context. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this citation.

OpenEval R20 evaluates claims C79-C80 (methodological principles with citations) and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these methodological justifications.

OpenEval R21 evaluates claims C81-C82 regarding PLD2's role in endocytosis and finds them SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims about potential confounds from expression levels.

OpenEval R23 evaluates claims C76-C77, C88-C95 (interpretive Discussion statements about broader implications) and finds them UNCERTAIN as they extend beyond direct experimental findings into speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative claims, though peer reviewers generally accepted the Discussion as appropriate.
